summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (74/135)

data.turoyo: Annaqla maskeno mḏ̣ayʕafwayle w hawiwa i ḥalayḏe hno.
data.translation: Nun war der Arme sehr schwach geworden und hatte seine Geisteskräfte nichtmehr zusammen.

rationale: First III Preterit-wa, provisionally retaining the reader's stem assignment; the expanded mḏ̣ayʕaf- form is flagged for paradigm review.

summary: New sense 2: trans. schwächen;
rationale: Jan 3.10/100 explicitly makes u stəʕmolo du lišono tərki the cause/agent and lišono səryoyo the affected object of maḏ̣ʕafle. This differs in valency and meaning from the inherited intransitive 'abnehmen, mager werden'. One clear attestation suffices; keep sense 1 unchanged.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (24/46)

data.turoyo: M bəṯr d fayət mədde d tloṯ əšne aʕle, u zʕuro kḏ̣oʕəf ġalabe w aḏəʕ ste, d i kačke ste, Səttəlbudur ste, ʕayni hiya ste bu ḥalawo yo.
data.translation: Nachdem darüber drei Jahre vergangen waren, wurde der Jüngling sehr schwach, und er wußte auch, daß es dem Mädchen, Sittilbudur, ebenso ging.

rationale: Fill I Infectum.1; explicitly prolonged deterioration over three years.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (44/53)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Ba, yabo, məs saymono? U papuko d ḥolux kafino. W ḏ̣aʕəf ġalabe. Lazəm d oxəl əšmo mede basimo. W hat ste harke hat a tre yawmani."
data.translation: Sie spraсh: "Was soll ich denn machen? Dein armer Onkel ist hungrig und ist schon ganz mager geworden; er muß Mal was Gutes zu essen kriegen. Und du bist ja auch schon zwei Tage hier."

rationale: Fill I Preterit Intransitive.1; hunger and current result of becoming thin.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (62/27)

data.turoyo: Məqqa d kəṯyo i ḥurma, koḥayro eba, i zʕurtaṯe, kal komaḏ̣aʕfo w kuyo ḏ̣aʕif. Məllala məlla: “Barṯi, qay hawxa komaḏ̣aʕfat w hawət ḏ̣aʕif?”
data.translation: So oft diese Frau kam, sah sie die junge Frau an: sie magert ab und wird ganz schwach. Da sprach sie zu ihr: "Meine Tochter, warum magerst du so ab und bist so schwache worden?"

rationale: Fill III Infectum.1; feminine second-person form in direct questioning, distinct from the inherited 62/25 statement.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (62/29)

data.turoyo: Qṭəʕle aw warīḏe d lebi, maz zuḥṯayḏe hawxa komaḏ̣aʕfono”.
data.translation: Er hat mir das Herzählen zerschnitten, aus Angst vor ihm magere ich so ab."

rationale: Fill III Infectum.1; first-person feminine and m-marked fear cause.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 3.10/100)

data.turoyo: Kḥuzena bəṯr maṯe baw walayat rabe u stəʕmolo du lišono tərki bu qərowo məqqa maḏ̣ʕafle lišono səryoyo.
data.translation: Of course, this was coming from the understanding that he had of Turkishness. Was this really so necessary? Did all the Syriacs know Turkish? Did they want such a thing? We see how much, after coming to these large cities, the use of Turkish in the reading weakened the Syriac language.

rationale: Only attestation of new III.2 transitive weakening; retain the overt causing subject and affected language.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.4/891)

data.turoyo: Harke stene səmlan ʕafro ġalabe, d lo əzze ḏoʕəf, məfqəḥ w lalʕəl ste, ʕafro ġalabe w ḥəṣolan ste ġalabe, kəmmət šeno. Yaʕni šuġlo d tloṯo yawme arbʕo yawme, hway amin, bale kule mloyo mlelan.
data.translation: Here too we put a lot of earth, so that it would not go weak and open up; and on top too, a lot of earth, and we also obtained a lot, as much as was good. That is, work of three days, four days, believe me, but we filled all of it right up.

rationale: I.1 Infectum has four examples after round 1; inanimate structural stability is an unusual participant extension and fills the cell to five.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.31/4943)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: U zabno bu zabno ḏaʕifo i ǧamaʕa, ḏaʕəf u ʕələm. Naqiṣi am madrašyoṯo, yaʕni lo bə ḥḏo naqqa hawyo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: As time went on the congregation grew weak, learning grew weak. The schools decreased; I mean, it did not happen all at once.

rationale: Thin I.1 Preterit Intransitive cell; overt feminine congregation and masculine education show agreement and institutional weakening in one context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.35/5582)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna lašan d foyəš u lišono ʕal i raġlo, haka ḏaʕəf ste, mən šira aw mən darbo gədobət laʕ ʕlayme d adyawma?
data.translation: Jan: Father, so that the language may remain on its feet, even if it is weak, what advice or what way will you give today's young people?

rationale: Thin I.1 Preterit Intransitive cell filled to five; weakening of language in a conditional question.

summary: I and III both describe intransitive weakening or weight loss. The attested III is not reinterpreted as 'make someone weak' merely from its stem number; its inherited gloss is retained.
Fear and grief occur as m-marked causes with a single affected subject (21/56, 62/29, 62/95). These are bodily changes caused by emotion; no special experiencer agreement is demonstrated.
I Preterit Intransitive ḏ̣aʕəf/ḏ̣aʕifət expresses completed change; ko-Preterit koḏ̣aʕəf at 43/32 emphasizes a visible result. Infectum ḏ̣oʕəf and III maḏ̣aʕf- describe ongoing worsening.
Spellings with and without an emphatic dot and the expanded mḏ̣ayʕaf- are retained. The latter supports a provisional III Preterit-wa addition but does not establish a new stem or sense.

Two inherited examples have consonants differing from the supplied full verses; exact-span corrections identify their existing example IDs. The inherited Russian note about a possible separate root is preserved pending verification, rather than silently removed.

Jan supplies a clear transitive III counterpart to intransitive I weakening. Do not derive a causative gloss merely from the stem number: the new gloss is justified by an overt causal subject and separate patient, while round-1 III intransitive evidence is retained.
Gradual hən bə hən and temporal accumulation occur with finite Preterit Intransitive ḏaʕifo, while kḏoʕəf presents ongoing weakening. The completed-change form does not entail an abrupt event.

ḏaʕəf yo with confidence or inner substance and the depictive ṭwiro w ḏaʕəf ḥzeli do not securely establish a finite Preterit Intransitive. An Arabic-type weak adjective remains possible; no Part act. box is fabricated.
Source emphatic and unemphatic spellings are preserved. These contrasts alone neither assign a different root nor prove a dialect boundary. Round-1 transcription corrections are not repeated.

At Jan 2.4/891 identify the exact implicit subject of ḏoʕəf; the earth-filling context suggests loss of structural firmness, without proving a specialized subsidence sense.
